newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Lawsuit ruling could cost Jamaica bauxite industry.
newsitem.headline: Lawsuit ruling could cost Jamaica bauxite industry.

text.p: Jamaica's bauxite industry on Tuesday faced the likely fallout of a local court of appeals decision which upheld a judgment against Jamalco obtained by a resident who lives near its alumina plant.
The court on Monday upheld a March 1995 award of $28,600 in damages to Herbert Broderick, who claimed emissions from the plant damaged his zinc roof on two occassions.

Lawyers for Jamalco -- owned 50-50 by Alcoa and the Jamaican government -- said they would appeal the ruling, which could prove costly for the industry. An appeal would be made to the British Privy Council, Jamaica's final court of appeal.
The ruling opened the door to claims from 40 other residents and damages could reach between $1.14 million and $1.71 million, officials said.

Justice Henderson Downer also recommended the government form a commission of inquiry into the problem of pollution caused by the industry, stating "a balance is to be struck between the economic benefits derived from bauxite mining and the environmental damage which is attendant on the extraction of bauxite."

The environmental problems stem from "red mud," a caustic effluent from alumina processing that must be stored in huge, lined ponds to prevent it contaminating ground water, sulfur dioxide emissions from the use of bunker C oil to run generators, and dust emissions from stacks.
The sulfur dioxide and dust emissions have for years been blamed for prematurely corroding zinc roofs in areas surrounding the country's three alumina plants.
The sector had gross earnings of $713.2 million and net earnings of $298.1 million last year.

Jamaica's alumina exports climbed to just over 3 million tons last year while bauxite exports held steady at about 3.5 million tons. The Jamaica Bauxite Institute said Brazil was likely to pass Jamaica as the world's third-largest bauxite producer this year while Jamaica would retain its number three ranking for alumina production.
